summary.intent: Finish and publish the checkpoint-based resumable version run work (PR #546 under a new trail), close the superseded PR #543, then act on a side note from a michi comparison by fixing Callisto's secret redaction ordering.
summary.outcome: PR #546 was opened ready for review with signed commits and local checks passing, and #543 was closed with a comment recording where its content moved. A fix branch for longest-secret-first redaction was committed, signed and pushed, and a new trail was created for it.

repo: Callisto work is organized as one Entire trail per outcome; a new trail is created with `entire trail create` and linked to a branch with `entire trail link`, and the PR number is then looked up via `gh pr list --head`.
The pre-push gate is a set of `just` recipes (pre-push, lint, doc-check, workflow-contracts) plus clippy on Rust 1.100.0 and `cargo test --workspace`.
callisto-model is MIT-licensed and cannot depend on the FSL-licensed michi-core, so michi code or logic cannot be adopted directly there.

Callisto's `redact_known_secrets` replaced secrets one after another with `.replace`, so a secret containing another could be left partly visible. michi-core's `redact_secrets` scans once, longest first, and is idempotent.
Callisto's `redact_token_shapes` (npm_, ghp_, github_pat_, pypi- prefixes, Bearer values, .npmrc auth lines) has no michi equivalent, but with one consumer it doesn't clear michi's gate 3.
Commits are expected to be GPG/SSH signed, and PR commit signatures are verified through the GitHub API (`commit.verification.reason`).

code.finding: `redact_known_secrets` was changed to redact the longest secret first so overlapping secrets are fully removed; a test named `a_secret_that_contains...` covers it. The transcript gives no line numbers.

workflow: The branch was created with `git checkout -b ... origin/main` while using a worktree, which swapped file contents back to main's versions. Files had to be re-read before editing.
The first attempt to close #543 with `gh pr close --comment` apparently failed or was unreliable, so the work fell back to `gh pr comment` and then a plain `gh pr close`.
Long PR and comment bodies are written to temp files and passed via `--body-file`, which avoids shell quoting problems.
A shared check script (`check3.sh`) is run against the worktree path before committing.

friction: Closing #543 with an inline comment took several attempts (close with comment, then comment, then close).
Branch switching in a worktree changed file contents under the tool, which forced re-reads before edits.
CI has not run on #546 and needs manual approval, along with Entire Gates approvals on several PRs.
open_items: Approve CI and Entire Gates on #546, #541, #542, #545 and release PR #533.
Watch CI and the Entire review on #546.
Clean up the spike and verification branches and worktrees after #546 merges.
Delete the remote branch for #543; the local branch with its unpushed commit remains.
Open the PR for the redact-longest-secret-first branch under the new 'Credential redaction in command output' trail.
Consider michi token-shape redaction only if a second consumer appears.
